Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

text:
The fed funds rate is 5.33%, so policy is still at its peak. The 10-year yield is 4.29%, the 2-year is 4.70%, unemployment is 4.0%, and core CPI is 3.41% YoY. US large-cap equity is up 26.5% over 12 months, and gold is up 21% over 12 months.

That points to mid-2024 or earlier. Core CPI at 3.4% fits either December 2023 or sometime in spring 2024. Unemployment of 4.0% fits January or February 2024, since it was 3.7% in the autumn of 2023 and 3.9% in early 2024. Headline CPI of 3.25% fits a spring 2024 reading, such as 3.3% in February.

Treasuries gained 2.2% in the latest month, so yields fell sharply. That does not fit February 2024 or early 2024 well, because yields rose then, and 10-year yields were about 4.0-4.3% in the first months of 2024. Core CPI at 3.41% is close to the February 2024 figure of 3.8% and the April 2024 figure of 3.6%, and neither matches exactly. A 12-month core CPI change of -1.92 would imply core CPI was about 5.3% a year earlier, which fits early 2023 (Feb 2023 was 5.5%).

The 12-month equity return of 26.5% is consistent with a window ending around the end of 2023 or in mid-2024. The 6-month return of 14.9% is high, which fits the period ending in April or May 2024 or the one ending around December 2023. Gold up 21% over 12 months and up 11.6% over 6 months fits a window ending in March 2024. But Treasuries up 2.2% in the latest month fits either November 2023 or December 2023.

For December 2023, the 10-year yield was 3.88%, so that does not match. For May 2024, the 10-year was 4.5%, and the 2-year was 4.88%. For the other candidate months, the 10-year yield was about 4.3% in the month ending June 2024, and the 2-year was 4.75%. Equities rose 3.8% in the month, which fits June 2024 (S&P up 3.5%). Unemployment was 4.0% in June 2024 (it had been 4.1%), and the 3-month payroll average was about 249K, which is plausible for a revised figure. The 2.2% gain for 7-10y Treasuries fits May 2024 better, since yields fell then (10-year from 4.68% to 4.51%). The 10-year yield of 4.29% in this snapshot fits June 2024 because the 10-year ended June at 4.36%. Core CPI at 3.4% was the May 2024 reading, released in June.

Headline CPI of 3.25% and core CPI of 3.41% fit May 2024 more closely. The 12-month change in the 2-year yield of -0.17 fits as well. I'll go with May or June 2024.
